profile.campus: Centeris South Hill campus, Puyallup WA (86 acres, 2 buildings: SH1, SH2)
profile.reading: Centeris SH1 Colocation is the operating first phase building on Centeris' South Hill data center campus, an 86 acre site in Puyallup, Washington owned and operated by The Benaroya Company, roughly 35 miles south of downtown Seattle. A November 2, 2017 Data Center Frontier article, reporting a 7 megawatt lease by tenant Colocation Northwest, operated by IsoFusion, describes SH1 as a 56,000 square foot LEED Gold facility, alongside a second building on the same campus, SH2, described as a 176,000 square foot powered shell, this registry's separate SH2 Build-to-Suit row, with an on-site substation supporting up to 50 megawatts of total campus capacity. This lease resolves an ambiguity an earlier pass on this row had flagged: the Colocation Northwest name found attached to a South Hill Data Center address on an aggregator site is not a separate, unrelated operator as that earlier pass cautiously assumed, but rather a tenant leasing capacity within the Centeris campus, explaining the naming overlap. That address, 1023 39th Avenue Southeast, Puyallup, Washington 98374, is applied to this row accordingly, now corroborated by an October 22, 2025 Data Center Dynamics report on the same property, which names it the South Hill Business and Technology Center and states current owner Centeris, still owned by Benaroya, invested nearly 200 million dollars over the prior 18 months to expand the campus to 24 megawatts of critical load including liquid cooled racks for high density, AI, and cloud users, with known tenants including ScaleMatrix and Chunghwa Telecom Global, and a direct connection to the Westin Building Exchange, Seattle's major carrier hotel and telecommunications hub. An earlier Seattle Times feature on the campus describes it as the first transpacific data hub designed to store and connect data between Asia and the US West Coast, built in 2008 and remodeled in 2011 in partnership with network provider Wave, totaling 376,000 square feet across its two buildings with nine backup generators activating within 11 seconds and a natural air cooling system. San Diego based colocation provider ScaleMatrix joined the campus as a tenant in March 2019, per regional economic development coverage, marketing itself as the first facility of its kind in the Pacific Northwest for high density colocation supporting AI, genomics, aerospace, and other demanding workloads.

profile.community_note: Washington State's 2026 Joint Legislative Audit and Review Committee tax preference review of the urban data centers sales and use tax exemption program lists Benaroya Capital as holding one exemption for the Centeris data center in Puyallup, Pierce County, describing it as opened in 2011. Separately, a City of Puyallup planning application, case PLCPR20220026, filed February 28, 2022 for the South Hill Business and Technology Center, covered an 86.67 acre parcel on 39th Avenue Southeast bounded on the east by Pierce College, describing current uses as office, warehouse, and data center, and proposed a rezone to Mixed Use Center with Urban Center zoning that would have allowed added residential and flexible uses. City records show the application was cancelled at the applicant's own request in May 2022, so the rezone never took effect and the site has continued under its existing data center use.

Per an October 2025 Data Center Dynamics report: nearly 200 million dollars invested over the prior 18 months to expand the campus to 24 MW of critical IT load including liquid cooled racks, a figure this registry treats as the current best public campus wide critical IT number since the report does not confirm how much of it sits specifically in SH1 versus SH2.

reading.body:
Centeris SH1 occupies 56,000 square feet within an 86-acre campus near Puyallup, Washington, roughly 35 miles south of downtown Seattle. The operator publishes 24 megawatts of critical IT load across the two-building South Hill campus as of October 2025, following a nearly 200 million dollar expansion focused on liquid-cooled racks. At 40 kilowatts per rack, a common density for AI training hardware, 24 megawatts translates to roughly 600 racks; at higher densities typical of advanced accelerator deployments the number would be lower. The on-site substation supports up to 50 megawatts of total campus capacity, leaving room for future growth beyond the current published figure.

The facility is LEED Gold certified and was remodeled in 2011 with nine backup generators and natural air cooling. Known tenants include ScaleMatrix, a colocation provider marketing high-density capacity for AI, genomics, and aerospace workloads since 2019, and Chunghwa Telecom Global. The campus holds a direct network connection to the Westin Building Exchange in Seattle, the region's major carrier hotel and telecommunications hub, positioning it for transpacific data flows between Asia and the US West Coast. It sits within Pierce County's urban data center sales and use tax exemption program.

Washington State has 46 mapped data center facilities and only 2 with published megawatt figures totaling 60 megawatts. Centeris SH1's 24 megawatts ranks it second in the state by published capacity. Washington's published AI infrastructure remains sparse by comparison to leading states, and gridside capacity constraints are not yet publicly visible in the state's operator disclosures.
